applicable_when: The kernel launches 3,920 CTAs with XBLOCK=128 on 132 SMs, producing 1 full wave + a partial wave of 1,808 blocks. NCU's LaunchConfiguration rule flags this partial wave as responsible for up to 50% of runtime. Achieved occupancy is only 47.7% vs 100% theoretical, and schedulers are idle 82.6% of cycles due to L1TEX stalls (62% of stall cycles). The kernel is a simple scatter-copy (load flat, store strided) with only 16 registers/thread. Larger XBLOCK values (512, 1024, 2048) reduce total CTA count: at XBLOCK=1024, grid=490 CTAs giving 3.71 waves/SM with no partial wave penalty. Wider tiles also enable better vectorized memory access and more instructions per warp to hide L1TEX latency.
